I just mixed it in with her clay to get her adjusted and she was unbothered. I'm not going to say that it's perfect and I can't smell a thing, but it is far superior to any clay I have ever used. My office/cat space smells like the lumber aisle at a home improvement store now which I don't mind at all. I change out the bag that collects her used litter every other day and I don't really smell much urine anymore. The automatic litter box seems to handle it just fine. It does get stuck in certain places but it's easy to scrape off unlike clay. The clay was getting stuck in areas that would trip the sensor and prevent the box from completing its cleaning cycle. I honestly thought I got a defective  bag.  I went to their website and it states that if the litter is not clumping, it is too wet from humidity.  I live in SW Florida.  Humidity capital of the world.  The website states the litter doesn't track (it does) and that it absorbs odor (it does not).   I scoop daily, and use pan liners to keep the smell down.

On the up side (proverbial optimist) I only put the litter in one of the three litter boxes.  We have three kitties and three litter boxes.  I am so glad I didn't put it in the lanai box (12 feet from pool) or bedroom (OMG, hubby would have a fit if he walked through this mess barefoot).  Our kitties don't seem to mind it (two kittens 6 mos old and one senior grumpy cat).  

I have never purchased a product that was so completely off from the description.  I switched to avoid the dust and mess from clay litter, but I'm running back to Fresh Step and begging forgiveness.
